name: eos-self-execution
description: Manages EOS self-execution loop: requirement processing, impact analysis, execution planning, verification, and evidence collection. Invoke when starting EOS self-orchestration work.
author: EOS Development Team
trigger: When launching the EOS SELF-EXECUTION frontier
When processing the first end-to-end real requirement
When building automation to replace manual coordination
When setting up agent orchestration for codebase changes

inputs: raw_requirements: object - Business/technical requirements to process
work_id: string - Target work item identifier
outputs: orchestration_report: object - Complete self-execution loop results
evidence_collection: object - All collected evidence types
governance_update: object - Updated governance state with verdict

preconditions: All required agent skills are available (recon, dependency-engine, verification, evidence-engine)
Requirements are clearly defined and prioritized

risks: Orchestration assigning incorrect agents to tasks
Missing dependency mapping leading to execution failures
Automated decisions bypassing required manual checks
risk_assessment.impact: High - self-execution is the core automation layer, incorrect orchestration breaks EOS ability to process work automatically
risk_assessment.mitigation: Mandatory dependency mapping before task assignment, independent verification of all outcomes, evidence chain validation before governance update

authority_boundaries: Can only orchestrate agent tasks, cannot directly modify implementation code
Can only write execution plans and reports to .eos-state/execution/
Cannot modify locked directories: packages/eos-core/foundations/, src/eos/semantics/
Must follow the canonical execution flow: REQUIREMENT → IMPACT ANALYSIS → EXECUTION PLAN → AGENT EXECUTION → VERIFICATION → EVIDENCE COLLECTION → DECISION → GOVERNANCE UPDATE
